message.content:
Let the legs of the isosceles right triangle be \(a\).

The hypotenuse is then \(a\sqrt{2}\).

The area can be found in two ways:

\[
\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}a^2
\]

Also, using the altitude to the hypotenuse:

\[
\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}(\text{hypotenuse})(\text{altitude})
=\frac{1}{2}(a\sqrt{2})(6)
\]

Set them equal:

\[
\frac{1}{2}a^2=\frac{1}{2}(a\sqrt{2})(6)
\]

\[
a^2=6a\sqrt{2}
\]

\[
a=6\sqrt{2}
\]

Now compute the area:

\[
\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}a^2=\frac{1}{2}(6\sqrt{2})^2=\frac{1}{2}(72)=36
\]

The answer is 36.
